evidence: batch_0038, after P-0008: the sieger still wins 70.7% [58.0, 80.8] and the spread is 36 points. In the same batch the team that secures Dragon wins only 42.5% of the time, and Baron 52.3%: at +1 AP a round, a Dragon card is worth less than the activations spent taking it, so the objective is not contested ground, and nothing on the map pulls the teams into each other.
hypothesis: The objective lever RQ-037a approved. Doubling what a Dragon card pays makes the first Dragon roughly a tower's worth of AP over a mid-length game and makes the second worth defending, so teams go to the pit, meet there, and the fight the game now pays for (P-0008) actually happens. That should cost the sieger, since time at the pit is time off the towers, and pay the objective and brawler personalities.
success_metric: In a personality batch read against batch_0039: the sieger below 60% and the spread between the best and worst personality below 25 points, from 36.
revert_if: The objective personality clears 65% (one dominant strategy swapped for another is not a fix), or median game length leaves 13-16 rounds, or win rate when Dragon is secured rises above 70% (the card deciding games outright), or games unresolved at round 20 exceed 5%.
side_effects: More AP in the game overall, so item timings move and the economy scorecard's 1.5x outliers may shift; the AREA engines are unaffected in kind. Dragon sits 1 hex nearer the South Nexus, so the South side may gain - watch the North/South split, which batch_0038 already had at north 60%. Baron is untouched, so the two objectives are no longer symmetric in value.

revert_checks.median_length: 18 -> 17 rounds, a delta of -1 on a baseline already outside 13-16

result.reading: The lever did nothing to behaviour and nothing to outcomes. Dragon takes per game did not move (2.33 to 2.37) and the same teams took them: the sieger takes 0.59 a game in both batches, the objective personality 1.8-1.9. The extra AP landed exactly where it should - the objective personality's base income rose from 3.74 to 4.65 a round - and the objective personality lost more, 47.6% to 40.5%. The team with more Dragons than its opponent wins 42% of games in both batches. 97 of the 120 paired games had the same winner. AP is not what a team in this game is short of: shop spend runs 11 AP a team-round against 2.4 on abilities, and the scorecard already records AP-cost abilities used in only 19.5% of the rounds they are affordable. A team paid more of a currency it cannot convert does not change how it plays or whether it wins. The objective lever, priced in AP, is inert; and Baron, whose payoff is already map-shaped (Empowered waves), sits at 47.7% when secured, so it is not just the Dragon. Nothing on the map pays back the activations it costs except a tower, which is RQ-037 restated from the objective side.
